headline: US midterms loom tomorrow, oil crashes 7% on Iran ceasefire talks, and Citi slashes lithium forecasts — a big week ahead for your portfolio.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO jumped last night as GTA 6 hype builds — the game officially enters its launch month with a November 19 release date confirmed. Investors are getting excited about what could be one of the biggest game launches in history. Good momentum for a long-term hold.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google bounced back last night after a rough stretch. News flow is noisy — Motley Fool analysts are calling it a 'genius buy' after a recent $505 billion market cap drop. The AI competitive pressure from Microsoft remains the main headwind, but the recovery last night suggests some buyers stepped back in.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara slipped again today after Citi slashed its lithium price forecast by 40% due to weaker battery demand. That's a direct hit to Pilbara's revenue outlook. The lithium market remains deeply oversupplied and there's no clear near-term catalyst for a recovery.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI dipped slightly today, consistent with some softness in the broader AI trade after October's volatility. Morgan Stanley has warned of potential further declines in semiconductor stocks, which make up a big chunk of this ETF. Nothing alarming for a long-term holder.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: DHHF edged a touch lower today in line with the broader ASX dip. Nothing stock-specific here — it's a globally diversified fund and today's move is just normal daily noise.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS slipped slightly on the ASX today, reflecting a small lag from last night's US session. The underlying S&P 500 and NASDAQ both rose last night, so expect VTS to potentially claw this back in the next session.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Minor dip today — nothing meaningful. VDHG holds a mix of global shares and bonds, and today's move is purely market noise. Long-term picture is unchanged.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was essentially flat last night after reporting strong Q3 earnings — it beat on both revenue and profit. Azure (Microsoft's cloud business) continues to grow strongly, and the AI story remains very much intact. A tiny dip after strong earnings is completely normal.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE barely moved today — down just 11 cents. Emerging markets have been soft broadly but there's no specific news catalyst here. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Citi slashes lithium forecasts by 40%
watch_today.detail: Citi cut its lithium price forecast by 40% today, citing weaker-than-expected battery demand. Australian lithium stocks slid across the board. Pilbara is already down 61% on your cost base — the investment thesis (EV-driven lithium demand) is intact long-term, but there's no near-term catalyst. Hold what you have, but be patient — this recovery could take years, not months.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 launches November 19 — the big moment is here
watch_today.detail: GTA 6 officially enters its launch month with a November 19 release date confirmed. This is the catalyst Take-Two has been building toward for years. Strong launch sales could be a major positive earnings catalyst. You're still down 9.7% on your TTWO position — a big launch is your best shot at recovery. Hold firmly through the release.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Bounced back after major selloff — long-term case intact
watch_today.detail: Google rose 1.38% last night, recovering some ground after what Morningstar called its 'worst day in history' recently — a $505 billion market cap drop linked to AI competitive concerns. Multiple analysts are now calling it a buy at these levels. You're down 8.25% on your small GOOG position. Nothing has changed about the long-term case — Google still dominates search, YouTube, and cloud. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: Oil crashes 7% — Iran ceasefire talks underway
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) plunged from $104 to $96.55 a barrel — a 7.3% drop — as Iran's foreign minister confirmed intensive talks with mediators aimed at ending the conflict. Gulf allies are still preparing for potential new strikes, but the diplomatic signals briefly spooked oil markets. Worth watching — if talks collapse, oil spikes again and inflation pressure returns.

watch_today.title: US Midterms tomorrow — AI regulation in focus
watch_today.detail: The US midterm elections are today (Tuesday US time). Goldman Sachs and major financial institutions are watching closely for signals on AI regulation — a divided Congress result is seen as likely and would limit big new AI laws. Markets expect limited direct impact either way. Former security chiefs have warned Trump could attempt to challenge results in Alaska, which a federal judge has already blocked once.

watch_today.title: Gold hits $3,977 — near all-time highs
watch_today.detail: Gold surged another 2% last night to $3,977 per ounce, driven by Middle East tensions (Iran conflict) and investors seeking safety ahead of the US midterms. If you've ever thought about adding some gold exposure to your portfolio, this is a good time to be aware of the trend — though at these prices, the entry point is much less attractive than it was a year ago.

world.summary: The big stories today: US midterms are upon us with concerns about election integrity; Iran conflict diplomacy is moving fast with oil crashing on ceasefire hopes; a major cyber breach hit Qantas and other airlines; and China's clean energy exports are reshaping global emissions data.

stories.title: US Midterms: Trump makes final push as former security chiefs warn of result challenge
stories.why_it_matters: Americans head to the polls today (Tuesday US time) for the midterm elections — the halfway-point vote that determines control of Congress. Trump made a final campaign push over the weekend, while a group of former US security and intelligence chiefs publicly warned that Trump could try to overturn results if his preferred candidates lose, echoing concerns from the 2020 election. A federal judge already blocked a Trump administration attempt to pause Alaska's Senate election. The world is watching closely — a change in Congressional control would affect everything from US foreign policy on Ukraine and Iran to AI regulation and trade.

stories.title: Iran ceasefire talks intensify — oil crashes 7% on diplomatic signals
stories.why_it_matters: Iran's foreign minister confirmed today that 'intensive contacts' with international mediators are ongoing to end the conflict with the US, though talks finished over the weekend without a breakthrough. The mere signal of diplomacy was enough to crash oil prices by 7.3% — from $104 to $96.55 a barrel — showing how much of oil's recent price surge was built on war fears. Separately, the WSJ reports that America's Gulf allies (Saudi Arabia, UAE) are still quietly preparing for a new round of strikes on Iran if talks fail. Iran has warned any renewed conflict could outlast the previous one. This is the most important geopolitical story in the world right now.

stories.title: Qantas and major airlines hit in large cyber breach
stories.why_it_matters: Qantas and several other major international airlines have been caught up in a significant cyber security breach, reported this morning. Details are still emerging, but airline data breaches typically expose passenger personal information — names, passport numbers, travel history, and potentially payment details. If you've flown Qantas recently, it's worth monitoring your email for any official communications and keeping an eye on your bank and identity accounts. This is a developing story.

stories.title: China's record clean energy exports slashing global emissions
stories.why_it_matters: A new report finds that China's record exports of clean technology — solar panels, wind turbines, and electric vehicles — have made a measurable dent in global carbon emissions. China is now the world's largest exporter of green energy hardware, dramatically cutting the cost of the energy transition for countries like Australia. This is good news for the pace of global decarbonisation, though it also underlines Australia's heavy reliance on Chinese manufacturing for its own clean energy buildout — a geopolitical dependency worth watching.

stories.title: Rubio denies Trump helped Bolsonaro flee Brazil to US
stories.why_it_matters: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio publicly denied that the Trump administration assisted former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro in fleeing Brazil to the United States, where he remains. Bolsonaro is facing criminal charges in Brazil over his alleged role in the January 2023 coup attempt following his 2022 election loss. The denial comes amid diplomatic pressure from Brazil's Lula government. It's a reminder of how US political alliances are reshaping relations across Latin America under the current administration.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 fell 0.58% today to close at 8,856 — a soft session weighed down by the lithium sector and broader caution ahead of US midterms. Last night on Wall Street, both the S&P 500 (+0.55%) and NASDAQ (+0.62%) had a solid session. The big story in commodities: oil crashed 7.3% on Iran ceasefire signals, while gold surged 2% to near $3,978 — close to all-time highs. The Aussie dollar is steady at 70.2 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Soft session — lithium stocks dragged, broader caution ahead of US midterms.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night: solid gains as earnings season continues positively. Tech led.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Last night: tech bounced, Google up 1.4%, TTWO up 2.5%.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Crashed 7.3% on Iran ceasefire diplomacy signals — huge move.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Near all-time highs — safe-haven buying on Middle East tensions and election uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Essentially flat. Holding at 70.2 US cents.

politics.summary: Australian politics is dominated by RBA interest rate fears — a widely expected rate rise is drawing warnings from state premiers and economists that it could tip the economy into recession. Westpac also dropped its full-year profit result today, and Labor is under fire over budget spending and new tax rules affecting housing investment.

stories.title: NSW Premier Minns warns expected RBA rate rise will close businesses permanently
stories.why_it_matters: NSW Premier Chris Minns came out swinging today against the Reserve Bank, warning that the widely-expected upcoming rate rise will see 'shops close that don't reopen.' It's a significant intervention — state premiers rarely attack the independent RBA so directly. Minns is adding political pressure on the federal government to step in. SMH is also reporting fears of an 'RBA-induced recession' if the rate rise goes ahead. For Gold Coast homeowners and business operators, this is directly relevant — another rate rise means higher mortgage repayments and tighter household budgets.

stories.title: Home borrowers face $6,000 annual hit as house prices tank
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR reports that the expected RBA rate rise could cost the average Australian home borrower an extra $6,000 per year in repayments — on top of the significant increases already absorbed over the past two years. House prices are simultaneously falling in some markets, meaning homeowners face the double-whammy of higher costs and falling asset values. This is the core economic tension the RBA is navigating: crush inflation without triggering a recession or a housing market collapse.

stories.title: Westpac posts $6.8 billion full-year profit
stories.why_it_matters: Westpac announced a full-year profit of $6.8 billion today — a solid result for one of the big four banks. Higher interest rates have actually been good for bank margins (the difference between what they pay savers and charge borrowers), which explains why the banks keep printing profits even as their customers struggle. It's a politically awkward result given the pressure on households right now.

stories.title: Labor's new tax rules risk housing investment — and there's a $170bn budget question
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian is reporting that Labor's new proposed tax changes — including tightening negative gearing rules on existing properties — risk scaring off 'much-needed' housing investment at exactly the wrong time. Separately, The Australian is also claiming there's a hidden $170 billion budget black hole in Labor's spending plans, an allegation the Guardian pushes back on, noting the government's spending picture is 'complicated.' With an election coming, expect this budget debate to intensify sharply.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is Google's Gemini 4 Carbon benchmarks putting it close to Anthropic's Claude — but at a better price. The US midterms are also generating speculation about what Congress's composition will mean for AI regulation. Enterprise AI adoption is becoming the key battleground between OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

stories.title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon nearly matches Claude in benchmarks — and wins on price
stories.why_it_matters: Google's latest AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon, scored just behind Anthropic's Claude in independent benchmark testing — but the kicker is it's significantly cheaper to use. In the AI world, being almost as good at half the price is a real competitive weapon, especially for businesses paying per-token (per-word, roughly) to run AI. This matters for your GOOG and GXAI.AX holdings — Google is staying competitive in the AI race and its cloud business can benefit directly from enterprise adoption of Gemini.

stories.title: OpenAI vs Anthropic vs Google: The enterprise AI battle is heating up
stories.why_it_matters: The big three AI companies — OpenAI (ChatGPT), Anthropic (Claude), and Google (Gemini) — are in an increasingly fierce race to win business customers (enterprises), not just everyday consumers. Enterprise contracts are worth far more because companies pay monthly fees to integrate AI into their systems. Google has cloud infrastructure and existing business relationships as key advantages; Anthropic is winning on safety reputation; OpenAI has first-mover brand recognition. This competition directly affects the value of your GOOG shares and your GXAI.AX ETF.

stories.title: US midterms will shape AI regulation — Goldman sees limited near-term impact
stories.why_it_matters: Goldman Sachs analysts say the most market-relevant outcome of today's US midterms is what it means for AI regulation. If Republicans gain ground in Congress, heavy AI regulation becomes less likely — which is generally seen as positive for tech companies. A divided Congress (split control between parties) is the base case, and Goldman expects it would result in limited new AI laws passing. For holders of GOOG, MSFT, and GXAI.AX, less regulation = more freedom for these companies to develop and monetise AI products.

stories.title: Argentina courts AI data centres with zero regulation and big tax breaks
stories.why_it_matters: Argentina's government is actively courting global tech companies to build AI data centres in the country by offering zero regulation and major tax incentives. It's a bold move — most developed countries are moving toward more AI oversight, not less. For tech investors, this signals that the global race to attract AI infrastructure spending is intensifying, and countries willing to offer the most permissive environments will attract billions in investment. It also shows how the AI buildout is creating major new economic opportunities across unexpected parts of the world.

sport.summary: The big NRL news is the Roosters winning the Grand Final 19-18 over the Knights in a thriller — a one-point margin at Accor Stadium. Off the field, the Rugby League World Cup is generating plenty of debate, and Benji Marshall has shaken up his Tigers coaching staff. In tennis, Brit Harriet Dart claimed her first WTA title.

stories.title: GRAND FINAL: Roosters beat Knights 19-18 in a one-point thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters claimed the 2026 NRL Premiership with a heart-stopping 19-18 win over the Newcastle Knights at Accor Stadium on Sunday night. One point separated the teams at full time — it doesn't get any closer than that. The Knights will be absolutely gutted having come so close to their first title in decades. A classic grand final that will be talked about for years.

stories.title: Rugby League World Cup: $40k player payment 'insult' and Kangaroos concerns
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports is reporting serious discontent among Rugby League World Cup players over payment — figures as low as $40,000 are being described as an 'insult' given the commercial value of the tournament. There are also growing concerns about the Kangaroos' squad depth, with columnist Crawls pointing to structural weaknesses that Ricky Stuart (Kevvie) can't easily fix. With the World Cup approaching, these issues aren't going away.

stories.title: Benji Marshall shakes up Tigers coaching staff ahead of 2027
stories.why_it_matters: Wests Tigers coach Benji Marshall has announced a significant coaching shake-up ahead of the 2027 season, bringing in new faces to his staff. Meanwhile, Broncos coach Michael Maguire (Madge) has sent a direct message to Brisbane fans — the details haven't been fully revealed but it suggests he's setting expectations for next year after a disappointing 2026 campaign.

stories.title: Harriet Dart wins first WTA title — Bartoli's coaching magic revealed
stories.why_it_matters: British tennis player Harriet Dart claimed her first-ever WTA (Women's Tennis Association) title over the weekend — a major breakthrough for a player who has long been knocking on the door. Former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli, who has been coaching Dart, revealed she pushed her 'beyond her limits' to get this result. Dart's win is being celebrated as a significant moment for British women's tennis.
